*UW–Madison · PSYC 752 Machine Learning*

Adapted from John Curtin’s Unit 4 classification lab and starter Quarto template. The lab supplied the cleaning workflow. This report documents the checks I reviewed and the data preparation used for my KNN and discriminant analysis comparisons.

## Data and setup

The course’s raw Titanic CSV contains passenger characteristics and a binary survival outcome. The course provided a separate held-out test set. This report uses the raw development data to create the training and validation splits.

To run the report, install the R packages readr, dplyr, stringr, rsample, and knitr. Put the course’s `titanic_raw.csv` in a local `data/` directory next to this file, then run `quarto render eda_cleaning.qmd` from the repository root.

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(rsample)

data_dir <- "data"
raw_file <- file.path(data_dir, "titanic_raw.csv")

if (!file.exists(raw_file)) {
  stop("Place the course's titanic_raw.csv in the data/ directory before rendering.")
}

data_all <- read_csv(raw_file, col_types = cols())
```

## Column names and variable types

I reviewed the coding against the course data dictionary. The two family-count fields get descriptive names, passenger class is represented as a factor, and the survival codes `0` and `1` become `no` and `yes`.

```{r}
#| label: variable-types

data_all <- data_all |>
  rename(n_sib_spouse = sibsp, n_parent_child = parch) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), factor)) |>
  mutate(pclass = factor(pclass, levels = c("1", "2", "3"))) |>
  mutate(survived = factor(survived, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("no", "yes")))
```

## Data quality checks

### Missing values

Cabin and age stood out in the original review. The data dictionary gave no reason to recode those missing values, so they stay in the exported splits. The modeling reports handle missing predictors in their feature recipes.

```{r}
#| label: missingness

missingness <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = names(data_all),
  missing = vapply(data_all, function(column) sum(is.na(column)), numeric(1))
) |>
  mutate(percent_missing = round(100 * missing / nrow(data_all), 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(missing))

knitr::kable(missingness)
```

### Numeric ranges

I checked the numeric ranges for values that might indicate coding errors. Fractional ages can represent infants, and large family counts and fares were plausible in the course data, so these values were kept.

```{r}
#| label: numeric-ranges

numeric_data <- select(data_all, where(is.numeric))

observed_range <- function(column) {
  values <- column[!is.na(column)]
  if (length(values) == 0L) {
    return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  }
  range(values)
}

ranges <- vapply(numeric_data, observed_range, numeric(2))

knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  variable = names(numeric_data),
  minimum = ranges[1, ],
  maximum = ranges[2, ]
))
```

### Categorical coding

I checked the survival, passenger class, sex, and embarkation labels. Names, cabin codes, and ticket strings retain their original formatting so they can be used for feature engineering. Embarkation codes are standardized to lowercase.

```{r}
#| label: categorical-coding

data_all <- data_all |>
  mutate(embarked = factor(str_to_lower(embarked)))

categories <- select(data_all, survived, pclass, sex, embarked)
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  variable = names(categories),
  levels = vapply(categories, function(column) paste(levels(column), collapse = ", "),
                  character(1))
))
```

## Training and validation split

The course workflow uses a 75% training and 25% validation split, stratified by survival, with a fixed seed. The outputs match the filenames read by [fit_knn.qmd](fit_knn.qmd) and [fit_rda.qmd](fit_rda.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: create-splits

set.seed(11151994)

splits <- data_all |>
  initial_split(prop = 0.75, strata = "survived", breaks = 4)

train_data <- analysis(splits)
validation_data <- assessment(splits)

write_csv(train_data, file.path(data_dir, "titanic_train_cln.csv"))
write_csv(validation_data, file.path(data_dir, "titanic_val_cln.csv"))

knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  split = c("Training", "Validation"),
  rows = c(nrow(train_data), nrow(validation_data)),
  survived = c(sum(train_data$survived == "yes"), sum(validation_data$survived == "yes"))
))
```

The RDA report reconstructed from the course HTML checks for uppercase `S` in its Southampton indicator. This cleaning workflow exports lowercase `s`. When rerunning RDA, check the port coding in the original modeling inputs before comparing accuracy with the reported course result.
